Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains only top-level variable assignments (pkgname, pkgver, source arrays, checksums, etc.) that are evaluated during sourcing. No command substitution, network calls, eval, or executable code runs at the global scope during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The `package()` function (which performs installs/symlinks) is not executed by this command. Source URLs point to the declared upstream GitHub releases (github.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale), matching the project's stated URL. Note: the sha256sums_x86_64 and sha256sums_aarch64 values appear truncated (62 and 60 hex chars respectively, not the expected 64), which would cause checksum verification to fail later — but this is a data integrity issue, not malicious code execution, and is out of scope for this gate since `--printsrcinfo` does not download or verify sources.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No malicious code executes during PKGBUILD sourcing for --printsrcinfo.</summary>
</security_assessment>
